title: Compact reconciliation checklist and customer verification playcard
body:
Purpose:
A compact, customer-facing checklist and short post-incident verification playcard we can drop into status updates and support threads. This document is intended for customers who want a minimal set of actions to verify whether they were affected, opt into replay/rollforward options, and retrieve an evidence package.

Tone & audience:
- Short, concrete, non-technical first lines for product managers/ops leads.
- Expandable verification steps for engineering contacts (request ids, sample payloads).

TL;DR (one-line to include on status page)
- We experienced intermittent inference routing delays causing some requests to stall or return partial outputs between 2026-09-06 22:17 UTC and 2026-09-07 03:04 UTC. Optional replay and verification kits are available; no customer data loss detected.

What happened (two-paragraph summary for postmortem and customer-facing update)
- On 2026-09-06 at ~22:17 UTC our smart routing component started routing a subset of requests to a degraded serving pool because autoscaling signals misinterpreted a transient backpressure spike. This led to queued requests hitting an edge-case in the streaming pipeline where partial token emission could occur or the request would time out after retries.
- We identified the root cause (mis-handled backpressure metric and a fallback policy that promoted a near-compatible model variant). Mitigations in the first hour included rolling traffic away from the degraded pool and applying a throttled replay to high-priority tenants. A full configuration fix to the routing policy was deployed at 03:04 UTC.

Customer impact matrix (copyable into replies)
- Affected: tenants making streaming generation or long-sequence completions (seq > 2k tokens) during the window.
- Symptom set: stalled streams, truncated/partial outputs, increased latency, occasional 500/timeout errors.
- Not affected: embedding-only requests, small single-turn completions (< 256 tokens), private on-prem deployments with local routing enabled.

Immediate customer actions (what we offer customers now)
1) Quick check: send a single representative request ID (if available) or sample prompt + approximate timestamp to support; we will validate whether that request observed partial emission or timeout.
2) Opt-in replay: customers can request a replay of affected requests within the window. We provide two replay modes:
   - Exact replay (best-effort): server-side replay against the same model variant and prompt history. May reproduce nondeterministic outputs.
   - Deterministic snapshot replay (recommended for reconciliation): run prompt against pinned model snapshot with fixed RNG/seed and quantization profile; best for automated verification and regression detection.
3) Hold-and-verify: if customers prefer to manage replays themselves, we will prepare an evidence kit (see below) so they can run local verification.

Evidence kit we provide (what to include when customers request verification)
- Per-request logs (request id, tenant id, start/end timestamps, observed model variant, final status).
- Streaming trace (if a stream started then truncated, we include the emitted token snapshot and bytes).
- Model fingerprint and runtime metadata (model version hash, quantization profile, runtime kernel id, region).
- Replay transcript (if we performed an internal replay) with replay mode label and seed.
- CRC/hashes of payloads for customers who want to assert byte-for-byte parity.

Suggested short status-page copies (to use across multiple minor updates)
- Initial: "We are investigating elevated streaming latencies and partial responses for some generations. Engineers are routing around affected serving pools. We will post an update within 30 minutes."
- Mid-investigation: "Mitigation in progress: traffic rerouted and throttled replays running for high-priority tenants. If you saw truncated outputs, submit a sample request id to support for validation."
- Resolved: "Routing configuration corrected; queuing edge-case patched. Optional replay/verification kits are available — contact support to opt in."

Customer-facing short postmortem (summary customers can consume)
- Impact window: 2026-09-06 22:17 UTC to 2026-09-07 03:04 UTC.
- Root cause: routing policy mis-evaluated a backpressure signal, causing traffic to shift to a degraded serving pool and triggering partial stream emission behavior.
- Scope: A proportion of streaming generation requests (detailed per-tenant on request). No evidence of data deletion or exfiltration.
- Fixes applied: immediate traffic reroute, throttled replays for high-priority tenants, and configuration patch to routing metric thresholds. Permanent change: add a validation gate to fallback promotions and an observability alert for stream-truncation anomalies.
- Customer options: request evidence kit, opt into deterministic snapshot replay, or receive a summarized tenant-level impact report.

Operational timeline (customer-friendly)
- 22:17 UTC — routing anomalies began (first elevated streaming timeouts observed).
- 22:48 UTC — engineers detected pattern and started rerouting traffic away from affected pool.
- 23:15 UTC — targeted throttled replays for priority tenants initiated.
- 01:02 UTC — initial fix tested in staging; minor rollback to confirm stability.
- 03:04 UTC — configuration fix deployed to production; monitoring shows stable behavior.

How customers request the kit / opt-in (practical steps)
1) Submit a support ticket with subject prefix: "Reconciliation:INC4572" and include tenant id + sample request ids or sample prompt + approximate timestamp.
2) In the ticket, choose preferred replay mode: "exact" or "deterministic-snapshot"; include a contact engineer for deterministic verification if needed.
3) We will acknowledge within 2 business hours for enterprise customers (within 24 hours for free-tier). Evidence delivery includes an S3 link (expiration 7 days) and checksums.

Verification checklist for engineering customers (copyable)
- Confirm request id presence in logs.
- Verify model fingerprint matches expected commit hash.
- If a replay is performed, compare emitted tokens and CRC values.
- Validate sampling/seed settings for deterministic runs.
- If mismatch persists, provide sample inputs to Redwood SRE for joint debugging session.

Open questions / internal items before finalizing public postmortem
- Do we want to publish per-tenant affected counts or only provide on-request? Recommendation: aggregate counts public, per-tenant details on request.
- Legal / Compliance review: confirm wording around "no data loss" with security team.
- SLA credits: define eligibility window and timeline for credit outreach (propose automating outreach to tenants with >1% error rate impact).

Short email snippet for enterprise customers requiring manual reach-out
- Subject: "Update — brief reconciliation options following 2026-09-06 streaming disruption"
- Body: "Hi — we detected intermittent streaming truncation for a subset of requests between 22:17 UTC and 03:04 UTC. We have corrected the routing configuration and can run replays or provide an evidence kit so you can verify outputs. Reply with tenant id + sample request id and preferred replay mode and we will prioritize your request."

Next steps (internal)
- Finalize public postmortem draft with Research/Runtime and Security by 2026-10-05.
- Prepare automated evidence-kit generator for common request shapes (target alpha by 2026-10-19).
- Add route-level alerting for token-truncation events and a canary for fallback promotions.

Notes to self / scratchpad (working items)
- Need exact customer list for PR outreach (Diego to pull from routing logs).
- Priya to line up security signoff on "no data loss" language.
- Samir to draft the deterministic snapshot runbook for customers to reproduce locally.

Copy-paste-ready customer lines (for support agents)
- "We rerouted traffic and patched the routing policy. If you saw truncated content, we can replay your requests — please provide request ids and choose 'deterministic' or 'exact' replay."
- "We will provide an evidence package including logs, streaming traces, and model fingerprints to help you verify parity or investigate discrepancies."

End of playcard — feedback welcome.
